key_insight: A symmetry-constrained machine-learning model predicts how magnetic orientation tunes the Berry-curvature dipole underlying nonlinear Hall response in a honeycomb model.
engineering_relevance: The approach could guide spin-tunable nonlinear Hall devices whose bulk dipole response survives averaging over equally populated, globally reversed magnetic domains under a uniform field.
method: Analyze symmetry, Berry-curvature maps, and occupation-weighted dipole contributions.
Fit a symmetry-constrained polynomial surrogate for both dipole components.
Evaluate spin configurations, chemical-potential sweeps, and fixed-carrier-density conditions.
evidence_signal: For 256 held-out spin configurations, both predicted dipole components achieved R² > 0.9995 at the reference chemical potential.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on carrier occupation and declines across the chemical-potential sweep, especially for D_y; transport predictions assume a constant relaxation time.
paper_title: Symmetry-Guided Machine Learning of Spin-Dependent Nonlinear Hall Response
